body:
### Problem

On exit, `vim.lsp`'s exit handler stops only the clients that `vim.lsp.get_clients()` returns. That call leaves out clients still waiting for the server's `initialize` answer, unless the caller passes the internal `_uninitialized = true` filter:

- the filter: [`runtime/lua/vim/lsp.lua#L1161`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/0851e7dabed9fc9c019e22088029f36e9f3ec3e3/runtime/lua/vim/lsp.lua#L1161);
- the exit handler calls `lsp.get_clients()` with no filter: [`runtime/lua/vim/lsp.lua#L1172-L1180`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/0851e7dabed9fc9c019e22088029f36e9f3ec3e3/runtime/lua/vim/lsp.lua#L1172-L1180).

So a server that is still starting when Nvim quits is never stopped. Nvim exits and closes its pipes, and from then on it depends on the server what happens. A server that doesn't exit when its stdin closes, or one that dies and leaves its own children behind, keeps running after Nvim is gone.

I hit this with tflint's language server (`tflint --langserver`). Quitting 100–120 ms after opening a `.tf` file left its `tflint --act-as-bundled-plugin` child running 6 times out of 6, still alive after 126 s; quitting earlier (before the client existed) or later (after `initialize` was answered) left nothing. In my config's CI, where a test opens a file and quits within half a second, it showed up as a leaked process.

I'm also seeing a process left behind after quitting with yamlls attached. I'm still investigating it and can't yet confirm it has the same cause; I'll add a comment here once I know.

Is leaving these clients out at exit intended? I couldn't tell from the code, so I'd like to check before assuming either way. Two things made me wonder:

- Other internal callers pass `_uninitialized = true`, at [L532](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/0851e7dabed9fc9c019e22088029f36e9f3ec3e3/runtime/lua/vim/lsp.lua#L532), [L953](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/0851e7dabed9fc9c019e22088029f36e9f3ec3e3/runtime/lua/vim/lsp.lua#L953), [L974](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/0851e7dabed9fc9c019e22088029f36e9f3ec3e3/runtime/lua/vim/lsp.lua#L974) and [L1059](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/0851e7dabed9fc9c019e22088029f36e9f3ec3e3/runtime/lua/vim/lsp.lua#L1059).
- `Client:stop()` already handles a client that is still starting: it terminates the server right away ([`runtime/lua/vim/lsp/client.lua#L928`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/0851e7dabed9fc9c019e22088029f36e9f3ec3e3/runtime/lua/vim/lsp/client.lua#L928), `if force == true or not self.initialized or …`).

### Steps to reproduce

A "server" that never answers `initialize` is enough, so `sleep` stands in for one:

```sh
nvim --clean --headless \
  -c "lua vim.lsp.start({ name = 'never-initializes', cmd = { 'sh', '-c', 'echo \$\$ > /tmp/lsp.pid; exec sleep 60' } })" \
  -c 'sleep 200m' -c 'qa!'
sleep 1; ps -o pid,comm -p "$(cat /tmp/lsp.pid)"
```

The `sleep` process is still running after Nvim has exited (3 runs out of 3, on both versions below).

The same run with those clients included, applied here from a user autocmd, leaves nothing behind (3 out of 3, on both versions):

```sh
nvim --clean --headless \
  -c "lua vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('VimLeavePre', { callback = function() for _, c in ipairs(vim.lsp.get_clients({ _uninitialized = true })) do c:stop(c.exit_timeout) end end })" \
  -c "lua vim.lsp.start({ name = 'never-initializes', cmd = { 'sh', '-c', 'echo \$\$ > /tmp/lsp.pid; exec sleep 60' } })" \
  -c 'sleep 200m' -c 'qa!'
sleep 1; ps -o pid,comm -p "$(cat /tmp/lsp.pid)"
```

For comparison, a client whose server did answer `initialize` (and, like the `sleep` above, ignores stdin closing) is stopped by the exit handler as expected when it has a numeric `exit_timeout`.

### Expected behavior

I expected quitting Nvim to stop a client that is still waiting for `initialize`, the same way it stops one that has finished starting. If that's not the intended behaviour, the change I tried above amounts to one line in the exit handler:

```lua
local active_clients = lsp.get_clients({ _uninitialized = true })
```

If the proposed fix looks okay, I'm happy to open a PR for it.

If it is intended, I'd be glad to know the reason, so I can handle it on my side instead.

### Nvim version (nvim -v)

Tested on both, with the same result:

- NVIM v0.13.0-dev-1868+gbe5167e21c
- NVIM v0.12.5

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

N/A (vim.lsp)

### Operating system/version

Linux 7.2.9 (CachyOS)

Related: #14428 (orphaned servers after exit, 2021, a different cause), #36783 (`Client:stop()` defaults to `exit_timeout`).

comment_data.body:
Following up on the yamlls process I mentioned: I've looked into it, and it has a different cause from this issue, so it doesn't change anything above.

In my case yamlls had already answered `initialize`. It was busy parsing a large YAML file when I quit. With the default `exit_timeout = false` ([`client.lua#L435`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/0851e7dabed9fc9c019e22088029f36e9f3ec3e3/runtime/lua/vim/lsp/client.lua#L435)), the exit handler sends `shutdown` and waits 0 ms ([`lsp.lua#L1178`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/0851e7dabed9fc9c019e22088029f36e9f3ec3e3/runtime/lua/vim/lsp.lua#L1178), [`#L1192`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/0851e7dabed9fc9c019e22088029f36e9f3ec3e3/runtime/lua/vim/lsp.lua#L1192)). yamlls only noticed once it finished parsing. It outlived Nvim by 4.2–4.5 s, then exited on its own, through stdin closing or its parent-process watchdog. So it's a slow exit, not an orphan.

I take that to be the expected result of `exit_timeout = false`, and I'm handling it in my config by giving servers a short grace period on quit. If that's not how `exit_timeout = false` is meant to behave at exit, I'm happy to open a separate issue for it.

> So it's a slow exit, not an orphan.

Yeah that seems reasonable.

>     I take that to be the expected result of `exit_timeout = false`,

Yes, the behavior of `exit_timeout` is well-documented I think.

A follow-up on the tflint child. I've been experimenting with a possible fix in my own config, and I'd like to check whether I'm going about it the right way before I go further. I haven't landed on a fix I'm confident in yet.

What I'm seeing: `tflint --langserver` sometimes dies of SIGTERM itself, before it can stop its `--act-as-bundled-plugin` child, and the child is orphaned. In a standalone probe (no Nvim, tflint 0.64.0) that sends SIGTERM 30 ms after `initialize`, this happened in 1 of 10 runs: the server exited with -15 and the plugin was still alive 3 s later. Otherwise tflint exits 0 and stops the plugin.

What I'm trying: `vim.lsp` starts servers detached by default on non-Windows ([`_transport.lua#L47-L50`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/0851e7dabed9fc9c019e22088029f36e9f3ec3e3/runtime/lua/vim/net/_transport.lua#L47-L50), [`#L60`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/0851e7dabed9fc9c019e22088029f36e9f3ec3e3/runtime/lua/vim/net/_transport.lua#L60)), so each server leads its own process group. `terminate()` signals only the server's pid ([`_transport.lua#L85-L90`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/0851e7dabed9fc9c019e22088029f36e9f3ec3e3/runtime/lua/vim/net/_transport.lua#L85-L90)). So in my config I'm killing the server's whole process group (`vim.uv.kill(-pid, "sigkill")`) when the server exits, and again at quit. In my repro, the plugin leaked 10 times in 90 runs without this and 0 times in 90 with it.

I'm not sure whether cleaning up a server's children is something Nvim should do at all, or the server's own responsibility. If a fix for this issue terminates servers that are still initializing, would signalling the process group make sense? I'd like to know the intent either way, and whether there's a better approach I'm missing.

To be clear about where this stands: the process-group kill I described above is something I'm still experimenting with, not a fix I've settled on, and I'm not sure it's the right way to handle this. The 0 in 90 is from one repro, with one server, on one machine. Caveats I'm still working through:

- A child that calls `setsid()` leaves the group, so this doesn't catch it.
- Process group ids get reused. Once every process in a group has exited, a later kill could hit an unrelated group. I compare the leader's start time from `/proc/<pid>/stat` first, but that only works on Linux.
- SIGKILL gives the children no chance to clean up. A SIGTERM to the group first, then SIGKILL, might be better, but it adds a wait at quit.
- Servers aren't detached on Windows, so this does nothing there.
- I get the pid by wrapping `vim.system` around `vim.lsp.rpc.start`, since the client doesn't expose it. That relies on an internal detail.

I'd welcome a pointer if there's a better approach I'm missing.

> * A child that calls `setsid()` leaves the group, so this doesn't catch it.

Nothing we can/should do about that.

Killing the progress group/tree is already handled by `jobstop` , which is why I want `vim.system` to adopt the job concept: https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/39552#issuecomment-4363910406

Manually doing that in the LSP layer is crap.

title: LSP: quitting Nvim leaves a language server running if it hasn't answered initialize yet
